title: Google Photos’ one-tap edit feature transformed my gray vacation snaps into photos worth keeping
excerpt: Turning average-looking vacation snaps into great-looking ones
content_html:
Published Sep 23, 2026, 6:20 AM EDT

Andy is a seasoned technology journalist with more than 15 years experience in the mobile industry, writing for Digital Trends, Wired, and more. 

Andy has reviewed hundreds of smartphones and tablets, dozens of smartwatches, and a host of smart rings, smart glasses, and fitness trackers, giving him a unique ability to assess and evaluate the latest products.

His daily mobile tech life includes Android and iOS devices, smart rings, and a smartwatch, unless it's a special occasion, when a traditional watch takes its place on his wrist.

Andy always has a strong opinion on the state of the mobile industry, and writes in-depth analysis features to put the latest news and products into context. 

He has attended multiple CES, MWC, and IFA tradeshows, has a passion for photography and cars, listens to far too much K-pop, and follows F1.

You can find Andy's portfolio of work on his Authory page.

When I took a long-awaited vacation, there was only one Android camera phone I wanted to take with me. The Google Pixel 11 Pro.

It impressed me so much when I reviewed it, I wanted to see how it performed in less familiar surroundings.

However, while the camera was brilliant once again, the weather on my trip was not. It was here a one-tap editing feature in Google Photos came to the rescue. If you haven’t used the AI Enhance button much, here’s why you should be using it more.

Quiz

8 Questions · Test Your Knowledge

Google Photos app
Trivia challenge

From smart albums to AI magic — how well do you really know Google's beloved photo platform?

FeaturesHistoryStorageAI ToolsSharing

01 / 8

History

In what year was Google Photos launched as a standalone app, separate from Google+?

Correct! Google Photos launched on May 28, 2015, at Google I/O. It was spun out from Google+ as its own dedicated service, arriving with unlimited free storage as a major headline feature.

Not quite — Google Photos launched in 2015 at Google I/O. Before that, photo management was bundled inside the ill-fated Google+ social network, which made it harder to discover and use.

02 / 8

Storage

Google Photos ended its free unlimited original-quality storage policy in June 2021. What storage cap applies to free Google accounts?

That's right! Free Google accounts share 15 GB of storage across Google Drive, Gmail, and Google Photos. Once you hit that limit, you need to purchase a Google One plan to keep uploading.

The correct answer is 15 GB. Google's free storage tier covers 15 GB shared across all Google services including Drive and Gmail. After June 2021, new photo uploads count toward that shared pool.

03 / 8

AI Tools

What is the name of Google Photos' AI-powered feature that automatically groups photos by the people who appear in them?

Correct! People Albums uses on-device and cloud-based facial recognition to automatically cluster photos by individual faces. You can name each person, making it easy to find all photos of a specific friend or family member.

The feature is called People Albums. Google Photos uses facial recognition technology to automatically sort photos by the individuals in them, letting you name and search for specific people across your entire library.

04 / 8

Features

Which Google Photos feature allows you to remove distracting objects or people from a photo using generative AI?

Spot on! Magic Eraser, introduced with the Pixel 6, lets you highlight and remove unwanted objects or photobombers from images. It uses generative AI to intelligently fill in the background, making removals look seamless.

The correct answer is Magic Eraser. This AI-powered tool debuted on the Pixel 6 and was later made available to Google One subscribers. It intelligently fills in the area left behind when you remove an object, producing surprisingly clean results.

05 / 8

Sharing

What is the name of the Google Photos feature that automatically shares relevant photos with friends or family members it recognises in your pictures?

Correct! Partner Sharing lets you automatically share photos that include a specific person with another Google account — perfect for couples or parents sharing memories with each other without any manual effort.

The feature is called Partner Sharing. It allows Google Photos to automatically detect when a chosen person appears in your photos and share those images directly with a linked Google account, removing the need to manually send pictures.

06 / 8

Features

What does Google Photos' 'Memories' feature primarily do?

Right! Memories surfaces photos and videos from the past — including 'this day' anniversaries, trips, and auto-created highlights — displayed at the top of the app. It's designed to help you rediscover moments you might have forgotten.

The answer is that Memories resurfaces past photos and videos based on dates and notable events. It goes beyond simple 'on this day' reminders by grouping themed collections like trips and celebrations, presenting them as mini highlight reels.

07 / 8

AI Tools

Which Google Photos editing tool uses AI to suggest brightness, contrast, and color adjustments tailored specifically to each photo?

Correct! Auto Enhance analyzes the content of each individual photo and applies AI-driven adjustments to lighting, color, and contrast. It's designed to make quick improvements without requiring any manual slider adjustments from the user.

The answer is Auto Enhance. This one-tap AI tool assesses the specific characteristics of a photo — such as exposure and white balance — and applies tailored corrections automatically, saving users from having to manually tweak editing controls.

08 / 8

Features

Google Photos allows users to lock sensitive photos behind biometric authentication. What is this protected space called?

Exactly right! The Locked Folder is a password or biometric-protected space within Google Photos where you can store sensitive images. Photos placed there do not appear in the main library, are not backed up to the cloud, and won't show in other apps.

The correct answer is Locked Folder. Introduced in 2021 starting on Pixel devices before rolling out more broadly, it keeps selected photos hidden behind device authentication. Importantly, content in the Locked Folder is stored only on-device and excluded from cloud backup.

Challenge Complete

Your Score

/ 8

Thanks for playing!

Is AI Enhance new?

No, but functionality varies on different phones

Tap the edit button in Google Photos on the Pixel 11 Pro and there are three Auto options immediately available: Enhance, Dynamic, and AI Enhance.

AI Enhance started out as a Pixel exclusive in 2025, but has since made it to most versions of the Google Photos app. Tap it, and AI works its magic on your chosen photo.

The feature differs depending on the version of Google Photos, and on different operating systems. For example, in iOS, AI Enhance generates three different edited versions of the photo. I’ve found it less effective than the one, single, master version made on the Pixel 11 Pro.

On the surface, AI Enhance sounds like a simple edit feature, as Google claims it enhances color and brightness. In reality, the AI looks at the scene more deeply and makes adjustments according to the subject.

Fixing problems the camera can’t avoid

The weather wasn’t on my side

During my trip away, the weather wasn’t very good. A mixture of cloud, rain, sunny spells, and overcast skies, plus time at altitude in low cloud, made it a challenging environment for the Pixel 11 Pro’s camera.

Most of the photos carried over the drab conditions well. While realistic, they weren’t especially exciting to look at, and sometimes you don’t want a reminder of poor weather.

In the image comparison galleries below, the original unedited photo is on the LEFT and the AI Enhanced edited photo is on the RIGHT.

AI Enhance added a degree of pop and visual punch back into the photos without going overboard. I don’t think the edits stray into hyperreal territory, which can happen with some filters.

Show, don’t tell

See the difference the feature makes

Sometimes, rather than using the manual adjustment toolkit on Google Photos, I just want to see an improved version of the image without resorting to a filter. This is where AI Enhance excels.

The photo of the reservoir above was taken at 5x and is a decent image, but give it the AI Enhance treatment, and it is transformed. The blue of the water is emphasized, the dry banks get texture and tone, and it better reflects what I was trying to capture.

It’s the same situation with the photo of the dam. The original lacks punch and vibrancy, and although it captures the impressive nature of the scene, it’s not very pretty. AI Enhance changes all that, infusing the trees with color, and bringing out the wonderful colors of the aged stone.

One of my favorite edits is another 5x zoom photo. It shows a yellow Fiat Panda Cross on a low bridge over a stream. I was happy with the composition, but not with the colors or the warning post at the entrance to the bridge.

Google Photos fixed all this. Magic Eraser took away the post, and AI Enhance amped up the colors. The tone is a tiny bit too warm for my personal taste, but this could be changed if I wasn’t set on a one-tap edit.

The 5x Portrait mode is still a winner

No matter the subject

The Pixel 11 Pro’s 5x telephoto Portrait mode can produce some great results, no matter the subject or the lighting. AI Enhance then brings out the best.

The first photo of the black Porsche Boxster S shows how accurate the portrait effect is, even when it’s not used with a person. The lines are sharp, but the blur is well-judged in the foreground and how it tails off towards the back of the car.

The AI Enhance edit does some interesting things. Outside the color boost, it adjusts the contrast levels to minimize the reflections on the glass, making the image more attractive.

Finally, we can see how AI Enhance recognizes subjects. In the photo of the cat, it adds a portrait lighting effect, and cools the surrounding lighting too. The photo was taken in lowlight indoors, and with the night mode active, demonstrating the 5x portrait mode's versatility.

One-tap convenience

Great results

It’s the convenience of the AI Enhance mode that makes it so useful. Sometimes, you just want an improvement without spending time editing manually, and AI Enhance delivers.

While I don’t think it’s perfect every time, and the edits aren’t always exactly how I would tune the photo, the results are usually very close. I’ll take that when all it required was a single button tap and less than 10 seconds to create the final image.

If you haven’t already, AI Enhance is a feature worth exploring in Google Photos. It took my vacation photos taken with the Pixel 11 Pro’s photos, ignored the actual weather, and delivered edits I will keep.

Published Sep 23, 2026, 6:20 AM EDT

Andy is a seasoned technology journalist with more than 15 years experience in the mobile industry, writing for Digital Trends, Wired, and more.

Andy has reviewed hundreds of smartphones and tablets, dozens of smartwatches, and a host of smart rings, smart glasses, and fitness trackers, giving him a unique ability to assess and evaluate the latest products.

His daily mobile tech life includes Android and iOS devices, smart rings, and a smartwatch, unless it's a special occasion, when a traditional watch takes its place on his wrist.

Andy always has a strong opinion on the state of the mobile industry, and writes in-depth analysis features to put the latest news and products into context.

He has attended multiple CES, MWC, and IFA tradeshows, has a passion for photography and cars, listens to far too much K-pop, and follows F1.

You can find Andy's portfolio of work on his Authory page.

When I took a long-awaited vacation, there was only one Android camera phone I wanted to take with me. The Google Pixel 11 Pro.

It impressed me so much when I reviewed it, I wanted to see how it performed in less familiar surroundings.

However, while the camera was brilliant once again, the weather on my trip was not. It was here a one-tap editing feature in Google Photos came to the rescue. If you haven’t used the AI Enhance button much, here’s why you should be using it more.

Quiz

Google Photos appTrivia challenge

From smart albums to AI magic — how well do you really know Google's beloved photo platform?

FeaturesHistoryStorageAI ToolsSharing

01 / 8

历史

In what year was Google Photos launched as a standalone app, separate from Google+?

正确的！ Google Photos launched on May 28, 2015, at Google I/O. It was spun out from Google+ as its own dedicated service, arriving with unlimited free storage as a major headline feature.

Not quite — Google Photos launched in 2015 at Google I/O. Before that, photo management was bundled inside the ill-fated Google+ social network, which made it harder to discover and use.

继续

02 / 8

贮存

Google Photos ended its free unlimited original-quality storage policy in June 2021. What storage cap applies to free Google accounts?

A5 GBB10 GBC15 GBD20 GB

这是正确的！ Free Google accounts share 15 GB of storage across Google Drive, Gmail, and Google Photos. Once you hit that limit, you need to purchase a Google One plan to keep uploading.

The correct answer is 15 GB. Google's free storage tier covers 15 GB shared across all Google services including Drive and Gmail. After June 2021, new photo uploads count toward that shared pool.

继续

03 / 8

人工智能工具

What is the name of Google Photos' AI-powered feature that automatically groups photos by the people who appear in them?

ASmart TaggingBFace MatchCPeople AlbumsDPhoto Groups

正确的！ People Albums uses on-device and cloud-based facial recognition to automatically cluster photos by individual faces. You can name each person, making it easy to find all photos of a specific friend or family member.

The feature is called People Albums. Google Photos uses facial recognition technology to automatically sort photos by the individuals in them, letting you name and search for specific people across your entire library.

继续

04 / 8

特征

Which Google Photos feature allows you to remove distracting objects or people from a photo using generative AI?

AMagic EraserBSmart BrushCClean ShotDObject Wipe

现货！ Magic Eraser, introduced with the Pixel 6, lets you highlight and remove unwanted objects or photobombers from images. It uses generative AI to intelligently fill in the background, making removals look seamless.

The correct answer is Magic Eraser. This AI-powered tool debuted on the Pixel 6 and was later made available to Google One subscribers. It intelligently fills in the area left behind when you remove an object, producing surprisingly clean results.

继续

05 / 8

分享

What is the name of the Google Photos feature that automatically shares relevant photos with friends or family members it recognises in your pictures?

ASmart AlbumsBPartner SharingCAuto ShareDSuggested Sharing

正确的！ Partner Sharing lets you automatically share photos that include a specific person with another Google account — perfect for couples or parents sharing memories with each other without any manual effort.

The feature is called Partner Sharing. It allows Google Photos to automatically detect when a chosen person appears in your photos and share those images directly with a linked Google account, removing the need to manually send pictures.

继续

06 / 8

特征

What does Google Photos' 'Memories' feature primarily do?

ABacks up photos taken on this day in previous yearsBResurfaces past photos and videos based on dates and eventsCCreates a daily slideshow of your most-liked imagesDGenerates AI captions for old photos

Right! Memories surfaces photos and videos from the past — including 'this day' anniversaries, trips, and auto-created highlights — displayed at the top of the app. It's designed to help you rediscover moments you might have forgotten.

The answer is that Memories resurfaces past photos and videos based on dates and notable events. It goes beyond simple 'on this day' reminders by grouping themed collections like trips and celebrations, presenting them as mini highlight reels.

人工智能工具

Which Google Photos editing tool uses AI to suggest brightness, contrast, and color adjustments tailored specifically to each photo?

AAuto EnhanceBSmart EditCPhoto TuneDAdaptive Filter

正确的！ Auto Enhance analyzes the content of each individual photo and applies AI-driven adjustments to lighting, color, and contrast. It's designed to make quick improvements without requiring any manual slider adjustments from the user.

The answer is Auto Enhance. This one-tap AI tool assesses the specific characteristics of a photo — such as exposure and white balance — and applies tailored corrections automatically, saving users from having to manually tweak editing controls.

特征

Google Photos allows users to lock sensitive photos behind biometric authentication. What is this protected space called?

APrivate VaultBLocked FolderCSecure AlbumDHidden Safe

完全正确！ The Locked Folder is a password or biometric-protected space within Google Photos where you can store sensitive images. Photos placed there do not appear in the main library, are not backed up to the cloud, and won't show in other apps.

The correct answer is Locked Folder. Introduced in 2021 starting on Pixel devices before rolling out more broadly, it keeps selected photos hidden behind device authentication. Importantly, content in the Locked Folder is stored only on-device and excluded from cloud backup.

Is AI Enhance new?

No, but functionality varies on different phones

Tap the edit button in Google Photos on the Pixel 11 Pro and there are three Auto options immediately available: Enhance, Dynamic, and AI Enhance.

AI Enhance started out as a Pixel exclusive in 2025, but has since made it to most versions of the Google Photos app. Tap it, and AI works its magic on your chosen photo.

The feature differs depending on the version of Google Photos, and on different operating systems. For example, in iOS, AI Enhance generates three different edited versions of the photo. I’ve found it less effective than the one, single, master version made on the Pixel 11 Pro.

On the surface, AI Enhance sounds like a simple edit feature, as Google claims it enhances color and brightness. In reality, the AI looks at the scene more deeply and makes adjustments according to the subject.

Fixing problems the camera can’t avoid

The weather wasn’t on my side

During my trip away, the weather wasn’t very good. A mixture of cloud, rain, sunny spells, and overcast skies, plus time at altitude in low cloud, made it a challenging environment for the Pixel 11 Pro’s camera.

Most of the photos carried over the drab conditions well. While realistic, they weren’t especially exciting to look at, and sometimes you don’t want a reminder of poor weather.

In the image comparison galleries below, the original unedited photo is on the LEFT and the AI Enhanced edited photo is on the RIGHT.

AI Enhance added a degree of pop and visual punch back into the photos without going overboard. I don’t think the edits stray into hyperreal territory, which can happen with some filters.

Show, don’t tell

See the difference the feature makes

Sometimes, rather than using the manual adjustment toolkit on Google Photos, I just want to see an improved version of the image without resorting to a filter. This is where AI Enhance excels.

The photo of the reservoir above was taken at 5x and is a decent image, but give it the AI Enhance treatment, and it is transformed. The blue of the water is emphasized, the dry banks get texture and tone, and it better reflects what I was trying to capture.

It’s the same situation with the photo of the dam. The original lacks punch and vibrancy, and although it captures the impressive nature of the scene, it’s not very pretty. AI Enhance changes all that, infusing the trees with color, and bringing out the wonderful colors of the aged stone.

One of my favorite edits is another 5x zoom photo. It shows a yellow Fiat Panda Cross on a low bridge over a stream. I was happy with the composition, but not with the colors or the warning post at the entrance to the bridge.

Google Photos fixed all this. Magic Eraser took away the post, and AI Enhance amped up the colors. The tone is a tiny bit too warm for my personal taste, but this could be changed if I wasn’t set on a one-tap edit.

The 5x Portrait mode is still a winner

No matter the subject

The Pixel 11 Pro’s 5x telephoto Portrait mode can produce some great results, no matter the subject or the lighting. AI Enhance then brings out the best.

The first photo of the black Porsche Boxster S shows how accurate the portrait effect is, even when it’s not used with a person. The lines are sharp, but the blur is well-judged in the foreground and how it tails off towards the back of the car.

The AI Enhance edit does some interesting things. Outside the color boost, it adjusts the contrast levels to minimize the reflections on the glass, making the image more attractive.

Finally, we can see how AI Enhance recognizes subjects. In the photo of the cat, it adds a portrait lighting effect, and cools the surrounding lighting too. The photo was taken in lowlight indoors, and with the night mode active, demonstrating the 5x portrait mode's versatility.

One-tap convenience

Great results

It’s the convenience of the AI Enhance mode that makes it so useful. Sometimes, you just want an improvement without spending time editing manually, and AI Enhance delivers.

While I don’t think it’s perfect every time, and the edits aren’t always exactly how I would tune the photo, the results are usually very close. I’ll take that when all it required was a single button tap and less than 10 seconds to create the final image.

If you haven’t already, AI Enhance is a feature worth exploring in Google Photos. It took my vacation photos taken with the Pixel 11 Pro’s photos, ignored the actual weather, and delivered edits I will keep.
